This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:古墳]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingdom|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == ### Kantō Region - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. ### Tōkai and Chūbu Regions - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). ### Kansai Region - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * Tanaka, Taku & Sahara, Makoto (2003). ''Nihon Kōkogaku Jiten'' (日本考古学事典). Sanseido. ISBN 4-385-15835-5. * Hirose, Kazuo et al. (2004). ''Politics of the Kofun Period'' (古墳時代の政治構造). Aoki Shoten. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:古墳]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. {{draft}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:古墳]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingdom|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * Tanaka, Taku & Sahara, Makoto (2003). ''Nihon Kōkogaku Jiten'' (日本考古学事典). Sanseido. ISBN 4-385-15835-5. * Hirose, Kazuo et al. (2004). ''Politics of the Kofun Period'' (古墳時代の政治構造). Aoki Shoten. {{draft}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:古墳]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingdom|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * Tanaka, Taku & Sahara, Makoto (2003). ''Nihon Kōkogaku Jiten'' (日本考古学事典). Sanseido. ISBN 4-385-15835-5. * Hirose, Kazuo et al. (2004). ''Politics of the Kofun Period'' (古墳時代の政治構造). Aoki Shoten. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:古墳]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * Tanaka, Taku & Sahara, Makoto (2003). {{draft}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:古墳]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * Tanaka, Taku & Sahara, Makoto (2003). ''Nihon Kōkogaku Jiten'' (日本考古学事典). Sanseido. ISBN 4-385-15835-5. * Hirose, Kazuo et al. (2004). ''Politics of the Kofun Period'' (古墳時代の政治構造). Aoki Shoten. {{draft}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:古墳]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * Tanaka, Taku & Sahara, Makoto (2003). ''Nihon Kōkogaku Jiten'' (日本考古学事典). Sanseido. ISBN 4-385-15835-5. * Hirose, Kazuo et al. (2004). ''Politics of the Kofun Period'' (古墳時代の政治構造). Aoki Shoten. {{draft}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:古墳]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * Tanaka, Taku & Sahara, Makoto (2003). ''Nihon Kōkogaku Jiten'' (日本考古学事典). Sanseido. ISBN 4-385-15835-5. * Hirose, Kazuo et al. (2004). ''Politics of the Kofun Period'' (古墳時代の政治構造). Aoki Shoten. {{draft}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * Tanaka, Taku & Sahara, Makoto (2003). ''Nihon Kōkogaku Jiten'' (日本考古学事典). Sanseido. ISBN 4-385-15835-5. * Hirose, Kazuo et al. (2004). ''Politics of the Kofun Period'' (古墳時代の政治構造). Aoki Shoten. {{draft}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == Related Articles == * [[List of kofun in Japan]] * [[Zenpō-kōen-fun]] [[Category:original pages]] [[Category:original pages]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Scallop-shaped Kofun}} [[category:kk]] [[ja:帆立貝形古墳]] ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)}}

{{draft}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == Related Articles == * [[List of kofun in Japan]] * [[Zenpō-kōen-fun]] [[Category:original pages]] [[Category:original pages]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Scallop-shaped Kofun}} [[ja:帆立貝形古墳]] ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)}}

{{draft}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == Related Articles == * [[List of kofun in Japan]] * [[Zenpō-kōen-fun]] [[Category:original pages]] [[Category:original pages]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Scallop-shaped Kofun}} [[ja:帆立貝形古墳]] ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)}}

{{draft}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == Related Articles == * [[List of kofun in Japan]] * [[Zenpō-kōen-fun]] [[Category:original pages]] [[Category:original pages]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Scallop-shaped Kofun}} [[ja:帆立貝形古墳]] ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)}}

{{draft}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == Related Articles == * [[List of kofun in Japan]] * [[Zenpō-kōen-fun]] [[Category:original pages]] [[Category:original pages]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Scallop-shaped Kofun}} [[ja:帆立貝形古墳]] ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)}}

{{draft}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == Related Articles == * [[List of kofun in Japan]] * [[Zenpō-kōen-fun]] [[Category:original pages]] [[Category:original pages]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Scallop-shaped Kofun}} [[ja:帆立貝形古墳]] ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)}}

{{draft}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == Related Articles == * [[List of kofun in Japan]] * [[Zenpō-kōen-fun]] [[Category:original pages]] [[Category:original pages]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Scallop-shaped Kofun}} [[ja:帆立貝形古墳]] ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)}}

{{draft}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == Related Articles == * [[List of kofun in Japan]] * [[Zenpō-kōen-fun]] [[Category:unsorted link categories]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:unsorted link categories]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Scallop-shaped Kofun}} [[ja:帆立貝形古墳]] ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)}}

{{draft}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == Related Articles == * [[List of kofun in Japan]] * [[Zenpō-kōen-fun]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Scallop-shaped Kofun}} [[ja:帆立貝形古墳]] ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)}}

{{draft}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == Related Articles == * [[List of kofun in Japan]] * [[Zenpō-kōen-fun]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Scallop-shaped Kofun}} [[ja:帆立貝形古墳]] ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)}}

{{draft}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped burial mound|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[Category:帆立貝形古墳|*]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese burial mound) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: 1. Circular mounds ([[Entfun|円墳]]) with rectangular projections. 2. [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these burial mounds reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == - '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. - '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). - '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}. - '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. - '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == - '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. - '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == - '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群}}. == Related Articles == * [[List of kofun in Japan]] * [[Zenpō-kōen-fun]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Scallop-shaped Kofun}} [[ja:帆立貝形古墳]] ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)}}
