{{draft}} {{Promising draft|reason=the high amount of work put into it over a long time, see edit history}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Scallop Kofun]][[en:draft:Scallop Kofun]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Scallop Kofun|Scallop Kofun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} with rectangular projections. # [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)}}

{{draft}} {{Promising draft|reason=the high amount of work put into it over a long time, see edit history}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Scallop Kofun]][[en:draft:Scallop Kofun]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Scallop Kofun|Scallop Kofun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} with rectangular projections. # [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)}}

Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} with rectangular projections. # [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)}}

Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Scallop Kofun]][[en:draft:Scallop Kofun]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Scallop Kofun|Scallop Kofun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} with rectangular projections. # [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)}}

Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Scallop Kofun]][[en:draft:Scallop Kofun]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Scallop Kofun|Scallop Kofun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ほたてかいけいこふん}} [[Category:古墳時代]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} with rectangular projections. # [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)}}

[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} with rectangular projections. # [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)}}

Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権|12=draft}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=draft}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=draft}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|12=draft}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=draft}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=draft}}

View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Scallop Kofun|Scallop Kofun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|12=draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} with rectangular projections. # [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市|12=draft}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=draft}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権|12=draft}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=draft}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=draft}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|12=draft}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=draft}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=draft}}

View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Scallop Kofun|Scallop Kofun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|12=draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} with rectangular projections. # [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市|12=draft}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=draft}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権|12=draft}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=draft}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=draft}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|12=draft}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=draft}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=draft}}

Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Scallop Kofun]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Scallop Kofun|Scallop Kofun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|12=draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} with rectangular projections. # [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市|12=draft}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=draft}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権|12=draft}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=draft}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=draft}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|12=draft}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=draft}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=draft}}

Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権|12=draft}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=draft}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=draft}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|12=draft}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=draft}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=draft}}

Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Scallop Kofun]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Scallop Kofun|Scallop Kofun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|12=draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} with rectangular projections. # [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市|12=draft}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=draft}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権|12=draft}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=draft}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=draft}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|12=draft}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=draft}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=draft}}

[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|12=draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} with rectangular projections. # [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市|12=draft}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=draft}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権|12=draft}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=draft}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=draft}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|12=draft}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=draft}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=draft}}

[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|12=draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} with rectangular projections. # [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市|12=draft}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=draft}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権|12=draft}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=draft}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=draft}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|12=draft}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=draft}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=draft}}

Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権|12=draft}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=draft}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=draft}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|12=draft}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=draft}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=draft}}

View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Scallop Kofun|Scallop Kofun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|12=draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} with rectangular projections. # [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市|12=draft}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=draft}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権|12=draft}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=draft}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=draft}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|12=draft}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=draft}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=draft}}

[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|12=draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} with rectangular projections. # [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市|12=draft}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=draft}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権|12=draft}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=draft}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=draft}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|12=draft}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=draft}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=draft}}

It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|12=draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} ({{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|12=draft}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=draft}} with rectangular projections. # [[Zenpō-kōen-fun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}} in {{ill|Kōryō, Nara|ja|河合町|12=draft}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}} in {{ill|Isesaki, Gunma|ja|伊勢崎市|12=draft}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichirō|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=draft}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権|12=draft}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=draft}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=draft}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|12=draft}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=draft}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=draft}}

Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|ja|ヤマト王権|12=draft}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=draft}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=draft}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=draft}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|ja|女体山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ota Tenjinyama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|12=draft}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=draft}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|ja|乙女山古墳|12=draft}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=draft}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=draft}}
