It was then deleted but preserved on everybodywiki. The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Scallop Kofun]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Scallop Kofun|Scallop Kofun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|[[:en:Otomeyama Kofun|Otomeyama Kofun]] ([[:en:Kawai, Nara|Kōryō, Nara]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]])]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by [[:en:Otomeyama Kofun|Otomeyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Kawai, Nara|Kōryō, Nara]], while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in [[:en:Isesaki|Isesaki, Gunma]]. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the [[:en:Yamato Kingship|Yamato Kingship]]’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''[[:en:Nyotaizan Kofun|Nyotaizan Kofun]]''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside [[:en:Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun]]. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''[[:en:Otomeyama Kofun|Otomeyama Kofun]]''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

It was then deleted but preserved on everybodywiki. The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Scallop Kofun]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Scallop Kofun|Scallop Kofun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|[[:en:Otomeyama Kofun|Otomeyama Kofun]] ([[:en:Kawai, Nara|Kōryō, Nara]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]])]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by [[:en:Otomeyama Kofun|Otomeyama Kofun]] in [[:en:Kawai, Nara|Kōryō, Nara]], while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in [[:en:Isesaki|Isesaki, Gunma]]. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the [[:en:Yamato Kingship|Yamato Kingship]]’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''[[:en:Nyotaizan Kofun|Nyotaizan Kofun]]''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside [[:en:Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun]]. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''[[:en:Otomeyama Kofun|Otomeyama Kofun]]''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

[[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11480883]] Wikidata name: scallop-shaped kofun [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:08, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created in the draft namespace on english wikipedia. It was then deleted but preserved on everybodywiki. The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to {{ill|Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion|en|Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion|WD=Q13429672|lt=Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion}} to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Scallop Kofun]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Scallop Kofun|Scallop Kofun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|WD=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|WD=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

It was then deleted but preserved on everybodywiki. The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to {{ill|Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion|en|Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion|WD=Q13429672|lt=Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion}} to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Scallop Kofun]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Scallop Kofun|Scallop Kofun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|WD=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|WD=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

[[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11480883]] Wikidata name: scallop-shaped kofun [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:08, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created in the draft namespace on english wikipedia. It was then deleted but preserved on everybodywiki. The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to {{ill|Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion|en|Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion|WD=Q13429672|lt=Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion}} to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Scallop Kofun]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Scallop Kofun|Scallop Kofun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|WD=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|WD=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

[[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Scallop Kofun]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Scallop Kofun|Scallop Kofun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|WD=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|WD=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

[[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] {{afc comment|1=to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Scallop Kofun]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Scallop Kofun|Scallop Kofun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|WD=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|WD=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

[[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|WD=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|WD=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

[[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|WD=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|WD=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

[[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|WD=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|WD=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

[[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|WD=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|WD=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

[[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|WD=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma|1=Isesaki}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship|1=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|WD=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun|1=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}
