[[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|WD=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma|1=Isesaki}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship|1=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|WD=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun|1=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

[[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|WD=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma|1=Isesaki}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship|1=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|WD=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun|1=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

[[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|WD=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma|1=Isesaki}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship|1=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|WD=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun|1=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

[[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|WD=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma|1=Isesaki}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship|1=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|WD=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun|1=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

[[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|WD=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|WD=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma|1=Isesaki}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship|1=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|WD=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun|1=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|WD=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

[[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|qid=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|qid=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|qid=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|qid=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|qid=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|qid=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|qid=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma|1=Isesaki}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|qid=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship|1=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|qid=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun|1=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|qid=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|qid=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

[[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|qid=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|qid=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|qid=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpōkōenfun|en|Zenpōkōenfun|qid=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|qid=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|qid=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|qid=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma|1=Isesaki}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|qid=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship|1=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|qid=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun|1=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|qid=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|qid=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

revision.text:
[[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[en:Scallop Kofun]][[ja:帆立貝形古墳]][[zh:扇貝形古墳]] [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|qid=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|qid=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|qid=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture|1=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Entfun|ja|円墳|1=Round Kofun|1=Round Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|en|Zenpō-kōen-fun|qid=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun|1=Zenpō-kōen-fun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|qid=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|qid=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara|1=Kawai, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|qid=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma|1=Isesaki}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Hirose Kazuo|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|qid=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship|1=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Wada Seigo|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|1=Seigo Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|ja|塚廻り古墳群|1=Tsukamawari Kofun Group|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|1=Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|qid=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun|1=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|qid=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|1=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|qid=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun|1=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Group|ja|馬見古墳群|1=Umami Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}

revision.text:
[[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|a scallop Kofun cgi]] {{ill|Scallop-shaped kofun|lt=Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11480883}} is a kind of [[Kofun]]. It is defined by a circular body with a small part extending. This can make it an interrmediate between a [[Keyhole-shaped Kofun|Keyhole-shaped kofun]] and a {{ill|Round Kofun|lt=circular-type kofun|ja|円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} ==Overview== {{Japanese-history-stub}} [[File:CG Otomeyama Kofun 2 7pbw.jpg|thumb|right|270px|{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|qid=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} ({{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|qid=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|qid=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}})]] '''Hotategaikei Kofun''' (帆立貝形古墳 or 帆立貝式古墳) refers to a unique type of [[kofun]] (ancient Japanese Kofun) characterized by a circular mound with a small rectangular projection, forming a shape reminiscent of a scallop shell. == Overview == This type of kofun can generally be classified into two categories, although distinguishing between them can sometimes be challenging: # {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Entfun|13=User:Immanuelle/Round Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} with rectangular projections. # {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|en|Zenpō-kōen-fun|qid=Q11268718|lt=Keyhole-shaped kofun}} with shortened rectangular sections. The first type is exemplified by {{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|qid=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}} in {{ill|Kawai, Nara|en|Kawai, Nara|qid=Q1203880|lt=Kōryō, Nara}}, while the second type is represented by {{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}} in {{ill|Isesaki|en|Isesaki|qid=Q328596|lt=Isesaki, Gunma}}. The first type emerged at the beginning of the Middle Kofun period, coinciding with the appearance of circular mounds featuring ritual spaces. These were likely added as ceremonial platforms.{{ill|Shiraishi Taichiro|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiraishi Taichirō|qq=}}, "帆立貝式古墳," in Tanaka and Sahara (2003). == Size and Structure == Hotategaikei kofun are characterized by smaller rectangular sections compared to keyhole-shaped kofun, and they exhibit a remarkable uniformity in size. For instance, the largest known example of the first type is 136 meters in length. In contrast, keyhole-shaped kofun display a broader range of sizes.{{ill|Ugaki Masamasa|ja|宇垣匡雅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ugaki Masamasa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Characteristics of Hotategaikei Kofun," in {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hirose Kazuo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11485567}} et al. (2004), p. 237. The consistent size of Hotategaikei kofun suggests they served different sociopolitical roles from keyhole-shaped kofun. Some scholars argue that these Kofuns reflect the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|qid=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingship}}’s regulations on tomb construction, indicating distinctions in status among local chieftains.{{ill|Seigo Wada|ja|和田晴吾|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wada Seigo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11418030}}, "Hotategaikei Kofun," in Aoki (1997), Vol. 6, p. 176.{{ill|Tsude Hiroshi|ja|都出比呂志|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsude Hiroshi|qq=}} posits that chieftains who could construct keyhole-shaped kofun were distinct from those who built Hotategaikei kofun, reflecting sociopolitical stratification (Ugaki, 2004, p. 235). == Examples of Hotategaikei Kofun == == Kantō Region == * '''{{ill|Tsukamawari Kofun Group|ja|塚廻り古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukamawari Kofun Group|qq=}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): Features four Hotategaikei kofun; numerous figurative haniwa unearthed. * '''{{ill|Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|ja|赤堀茶臼山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Akabori Chausuyama Kofun|qq=}}''' (Isesaki City, Gunma Prefecture): Contains diverse haniwa (chairs, buildings, etc.). * '''{{ill|Nyotaizan Kofun|en|Nyotaizan Kofun|qid=Q17229664|lt=Nyotaizan Kofun}}''' (Ōta City, Gunma Prefecture): 106 meters long, planned alongside {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|qid=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}. * '''Rai Denyama Kofun''' (Higashimatsuyama City, Saitama Prefecture): Earliest kofun featuring haniwa in Saitama. * '''{{ill|Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Noge Ōtsuka Kofun|lt=Nogeotsuka Kofun|ja|野毛大塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nogeotsuka Kofun|qq=}}''' (Setagaya Ward, Tokyo): Diameter of 66 meters, one of the largest Hotategaikei kofun in Eastern Japan. == Tōkai and Chūbu Regions == * '''{{ill|Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja|王子塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōji Tsuka Kofun|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}''' (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture): 50.8 meters long; mid-5th to early 6th century. * '''Noshi Kofun Cluster, Tomb 7''' (Ōno Town, Gifu Prefecture). == Kansai Region == * '''{{ill|Otomeyama Kofun|en|Otomeyama Kofun|qid=Q11369896|lt=Otomeyama Kofun}}''' (Kōryō, Nara): 135 meters long, part of the {{ill|Umami Kofun Cluster|ja|馬見古墳群|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Group|13=User:Immanuelle/Umami Kofun Cluster|qq=}}. ==List== * {{ill|Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|ja|青塚古墳 (観音寺市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aozuka Kofun (Kannonji City)|qq=}}
